text.p: Here are the highligts of stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
POLITIKA
- June average wage of 807 dinars was in real terms up by one third on June wages the previous year.
- Some 57 percent of total number of employed receive lower wage than the average and 19.5 percent live on the verge of poverty, the Institute for Market Research said.

- Implementation of the laws on ownership transformation, concessions and joint investment should secure over $2 billion by the end of next year, said vice-president of the Serbian Chamber of Commerce Momir Pavlicevic.
- Serbia will not allow meat imports nor increase of prices as there is no justified reason for that, said the republic's Agriculture Minister Jovan Babovic.
- Vuk Draskovic, leader of the opposition Serbian Renewal Movement (SPO), said boycott of upcoming Serbian presidental and parliamentary elections was directed against SPO.
- Two Kosovo ethnic Albanians killed in an incident on Yugoslav-Albanian border.
NASA BORBA

- Solution of the present political crisis in the Bosnian Serb Republic expected after a visit of former special U.S. envoy for ex-Yugoslavia Richard Holbrooke on August 8 and Constitutional Court decision on August 10.
- The Democratic Party of Serbia calls for boycott of Serbia's parliamentary and presidental elections at all costs.
- Election lists for 250 Serbian parliament members to be submitted by September 6.
- Student movement of Serbia to launch anti-election campaign from August 15 to September 15.
- Zoran Djindjic, president of the Democratic Party, says the party will not run in September 21 elections.
- Montenegrin State Prosecutor Vladimir Susovic said the Hague war crimes tribunal interested in republican President Momir Bulatovic's role during war operations near Dubrovnik.
- Montenegrin Trade Minister Branko Vujovic said border blockade between Serbia and Montenegro was gaining proportions of an economic war between the two Yugoslav republics.
- Yugoslav companies' net losses will probably rise by another six billion dinars or one third of the total losses of 17.5 billion dinars incurred in 1996, said economist Jovan Rankovic.
BORBA
- Frequent and heavy rains threat to sunflower crop, said Dragan Skoric of the Novi Sad Institute for Vegetable and Crop Farming.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA

- We should hope the federal government will respond positively to the European Union message and finally opt for democratic development, economic revival and integration to the international community, said the paper's commentary.

- Serbia failed to make attractive climate for privatisation and foreign investments which will reflect on the privatisation process in Montenegro, the paper said. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
